newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Nearby robusta coffee futures ended easier but forwards were slightly firmer on industry buying with switches dominating most of the session's activity. November lost $1.00 to close at $1,505 while January closed $4.00 higher at $1,452 a tonne.

In New York arabica futures eased again and came close to levels that might trigger additional technical sell signals. However, low consumer stocks should prevent the market from dropping too sharply. But, with new crop supplies coming onto the market, the concern over low consumer stocks is not that great. Problems in Colombia have apparently subsided and there do not seem to be any delays in shipments because of rebel attacks.

ACPC - ACPC countries exported 44.837 million 60-kg bags of green coffee in 1995/96 (July/June) against a target of 45.841 million tonnes, ACPC sources said. The shortfall of 2.19 per cent should not have any impact on prices. As anticipated the one-day meeting made no major policy revisions and ACPC officials said the 14-member grouping would maintain its exisiting export program.

The ACPC last met in May when it agreed a new plan to limit green coffee exports from its members to 53.5 million bags in 1996/97. However, ACPC secretary general Robeiro Oliveira Silva said he did not discount the possibility of revising supply controls if prices continue to tumble.

GUATEMALA - Guatemala's 1996/97 (October/September) coffee harvest is facing delays after heavy rains this year. It was said delays of about one month appeared likely for the harvest on the Pacific side of the country and other regions could be similarly affected. The heavy rains, which caused late flowering, are unlikely to affect quantity or quality, industry sources said. It is expected that production in 1996/97 will be at around last year's level of 3.3 million 60- kg bags.

INDONESIA - Indonesian coffee production in coffee year 1997/98 (October/September) is expected to reach 8.3 million 60-kg bags up from an estimated 8.0 million bags in 1996/97, Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters told Reuters. However, he did not give any figures for crop year 1996/97 (April/March).

FINLAND - Finland imported 113,302 bags of coffee in April 1996, signficantly up on last year's figure of 60,496 bags. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 314,400 bags, 23 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 44 per cent to 758,500 bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/April 1996 were Guatemala (40,000 vs 36,400 bags), Brazil (48,300 vs 52,600 bags) and Colombia (92,600 vs 65,400 bags).

The country exported 44,200 bags of coffee in January/April 1996, 52 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply to 96,800 bags from 217,500 bags the previous year.
